title: What Savitri told Death
hook: Savitri has no weapon on the road behind Death, only words about the company of the good
carry: satsang: time near the good is never wasted

segments.voice: Yesterday, a vrata, a fast held as prayer for someone: in the hermitage, Savitri carried Narada's warning alone, counted the days, and fasted three nights.
screen: `A VRATA: A FAST HELD AS PRAYER FOR SOMEONE.`

segments.voice: No sword. No army. No spell. When Yama, the lord of death, draws Satyavan's life out of his body and turns south, Savitri has nothing to fight with. What she has is a voice. She walks behind Death and talks, and again and again, Death stops to listen. Last year we followed the boons one by one. Today we listen to what she actually says, because that's what moves him.
screen: `NO SWORD, NO ARMY.` → `SHE WALKS AND TALKS.` → `DEATH STOPS TO LISTEN.`

segments.voice: Yama tells her to turn back. Her first answer is about where she belongs: where her husband is taken, she goes. Then she speaks of friendship. The wise say, she tells him, that walking seven steps together makes people friends, and she has walked more than that beside him. She doesn't plead with Death as an enemy. She claims him as a companion on the road. Then she speaks of dharma, and of the good, the people who keep to it. Yama is pleased and offers a gift, anything but Satyavan's life. She asks for her father-in-law's sight. She keeps talking: being near the good, even for a moment, is never wasted. Another gift: her father-in-law's kingdom. The good are kind even to those who wrong them, she says. Another gift: sons for her own father. And the good, she says, hold the world up by their truth. Each time, what pleases Yama is not grief and not cleverness. It's what she says about goodness. Here's the teaching she's pointing at, one Hindus prize: satsang, the company of the good. Being near holy and good people is held to change you, slowly, the way sitting near a fire warms you. It's why Hindus gather at the temple for bhajans and talks, why families sit together for a reading, why a visit to a holy person is called a blessing. This is a week's end, so look back. Kunti walked into vanaprastha. Gandhari blessed dharma over her own side, bound her eyes, and poured water for her sons. Savitri, named for the Gayatri, kept a vow, and now speaks of the good to Death himself.
screen: `SEVEN STEPS MAKE A FRIEND` · `NEAR THE GOOD IS NEVER WASTED` · `SATSANG: THE COMPANY OF THE GOOD` · `A CONVERSATION DEATH ENJOYS`

segments.voice: Call to mind someone whose goodness you've seen up close, not famous, just good, and one small kind thing they did that nobody else noticed. Sit near them in your mind for a few breaths, the way Savitri says the good are worth being near, and let a little of it rub off. If you pray, you can give thanks for them; this week, you might find a way to spend real time near them.
Savitri. The woman who walked behind Death and spoke about the good until he gave her what she asked. Today's word.
Your line: satsang, time near the good is never wasted. Savitri told Death so. Same time tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus gather for satsang, the company of the good, at temples and in homes, for bhajans, readings and talks; Savitri's words to Yama are heard when her story is retold, and on the day of the vow some married women keep in her name.

original.note: Sanskrit: the princess's name, the same as the goddess who granted her birth and the verse to the sun god Savitr.

trapdoor: what you thought: Savitri tricked Death.
what it means: she spoke of dharma and the company of the good, satsang, and he was pleased each time.
what a scholar hears: in the epic, every gift follows a speech about the good, and the first three go to her elders.
